newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt further privatises steel firm.
newsitem.headline: Egypt further privatises steel firm.

text.p: The Egyptian state on Saturday offered investors at least 500,000 shares or 7.14 percent of its holding in partly privatised Alexandria National Iron and Steel (ANSDK).

The state-run National Investment Bank said in an announcement that the offer would open on Tuesday May 27 and close on Monday June 2. Investors can bid for the shares from a floor price of 260.78 pounds, the stock's closing price on the bourse on Thursday.

Al-Salam brokerage and the Alexandria-based International Brokerage are also handling the sale, which comes during the government's recent acceleration of its privatisation programme, flagship of the state's economic reforms.
The state owns 64.52 percent of ANSDK, while the employee shareholder association and private investors hold 13.83 percent.
Mutual funds own 6.61 percent, World Bank affiliate the International Finance Corporation (IFC) 5.00 percent and unidentified Japanese firms hold the remaining 10.04 percent.

ANSDK also signed on Thursday a deal with German firm Messer Griesheim to set up a $25 million joint venture firm to produce industrial gases with investment from the IFC. Messer Griesheim is a unit of Hoechst AG.

ANSDK said in the announcement it had increased net profits for calendar 1996 to 122.7 million pounds ($36.15 million) from 120.5 million in the previous year. Net sales fell to 1.32 billion pounds from 1.53 billion in 1995 while dividends per share remained the same at 10 pounds.
ANSDK has a total of seven million shares with a nominal value of 100 pounds per share.
